It treats the existing institutional structure (the 'Administrative State') as an illegitimate obstacle to the movement's will, rather than a set of neutral democratic guardrails.

concepts.quote: Progressive elites speak in lofty terms of openness, progress, expertise, cooperation, and globalization. But too often, these terms are just rhetorical Trojan horses concealing their true intention—stripping “we the people” of our constitutional authority over our country’s future.
concepts.explanation: The text frames the 'People' as a monolithic entity whose authority is being stolen by a specific, illegitimate 'elite' class. It treats 'expertise' and 'cooperation' not as valid concepts but as deceptive tools ('Trojan horses') used by an enemy of the 'People.' This aligns with Eco's description of the leader/movement interpreting the 'Common Will' against 'delegated' or 'expert' institutions.

concepts.quote: Instead, they believe in a kind of 21st century Wilsonian order in which the “enlightened,” highly educated managerial elite runs things rather than the humble, patriotic working families who make up the majority of what the elites contemptuously call “fly-over country.”
concepts.explanation: This passage explicitly weaponizes status anxiety and feelings of political and social humiliation. It contrasts the 'enlightened' elite with 'humble, patriotic working families' and uses the term 'fly-over country' to highlight the perceived disdain and humiliation directed at the middle class by those above them.

concepts.quote: This Wilsonian hubris has spread like a cancer through many of America’s largest corporations, its public institutions, and its popular culture. Those who run our so-called American corporations have bent to the will of the woke agenda and care more for their foreign investors and organizations than their American workers and customers.
concepts.explanation: The text uses the metaphor of 'cancer' to describe an internal ideological shift and frames corporate leaders as being in league with 'foreign' interests against the national body. It suggests a coordinated subversion ('bent to the will') rather than simple market forces or policy shifts, implying a plot involving both internal traitors and external enemies.

concepts.quote: Today, nearly every top-tier U.S. university president or Wall Street hedge fund manager has more in common with a socialist, European head of state than with the parents at a high school football game in Waco, Texas.
concepts.explanation: This creates a sharp 'us vs. them' dichotomy based on cultural and national identity. It frames the 'elite' as 'other' (socialist, European) and therefore alien to the 'real' American identity (parents in Waco). It treats cultural and ideological difference as a form of national contamination or betrayal of the 'authentic' citizenry.
